GA-2025-SB160.title: Reckless Stunt Driving; a motor vehicle involved in a second offense of reckless stunt driving; replace the forfeiture penalty
GA-2025-SB160.summary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend Code Section 40-6-390.1 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to reckless stunt driving, so as to replace the forfeiture penalty of a motor vehicle involved in a second offense of reckless stunt driving with authority to order the installation of a device which limits the speed of such vehicle; to provide for a definition; to provide for procedures and conditions upon issuance of such orders; to provide for notification to the Department of Revenue; to provide for a penalty; to provide for related matters; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.

GA-2025-SB160.policyArea: MOTOR VEHICLES AND TRAFFIC, PENAL INSTITUTIONS, PROFESSIONS AND BUSINESSES
GA-2025-SB160.aiSummary: This law changes the penalty for a second reckless stunt driving offense by letting a court order a device that limits a vehicle’s speed instead of taking the vehicle away. It also sets rules for when that order can be used, tells the Department of Revenue, and takes effect July 1, 2028.

GA-2025-SB384.title: Motor Vehicle; optional five-year motor vehicle registration and revalidation for certain motor vehicles; provide
GA-2025-SB384.summary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend Article 2 of Chapter 9 of Title 12 and Title 40 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to motor vehicle emission inspection and maintenance and motor vehicles and traffic, respectively, so as to provide for an optional five-year motor vehicle registration and revalidation for certain motor vehicles; to revise and provide for definitions; to provide for conforming changes; to provide for related matters; to provide for an effective date; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.

actions.text: Senate Committee Favorably Reported By Substitute

GA-2025-SB384.aiSummary: Georgia law now lets some vehicle owners choose a five-year registration and revalidation period instead of a shorter one. It also updates related legal terms and makes matching changes in the state motor vehicle laws. The law takes effect on July 1, 2027.

GA-2025-SB524.title: License Plates; specialty license plate honoring Girl Scouts of Georgia; establish
GA-2025-SB524.summary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend Code Section 40-2-86 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to license plates promoting or supporting certain agencies, funds, or nonprofit corporations with proceeds disbursed to the general fund and the agency, fund, or nonprofit corporation, so as to establish a specialty license plate honoring Girl Scouts of Georgia; to establish a specialty plate honoring the 250th anniversary of the United States of America's independence; to provide for related matters; to provide for compliance with constitutional requirements; to provide for an effective date; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.
committees: House Public Safety and Homeland Security

actions.text: Senate Committee Favorably Reported By Substitute

GA-2025-SB524.aiSummary: The law creates special Georgia license plates, including one honoring Girl Scouts of Georgia and one marking the 250th anniversary of the United States. It changes state rules for these plates and related payments. It became law in 2026 and takes effect on January 1, 2027.

GA-2025-HB90.title: Revenue and taxation; increase maximum acreage to qualify for assessment and taxation as a bona fide conservation use property
GA-2025-HB90.summary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend Code Section 48-5-7.4 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to preferential assessment for bona fide conservation use property and bona fide residential transitional property, so as to increase the maximum acreage to qualify for assessment and taxation as a bona fide conservation use property; to provide for related matters; to provide for a contingent effective date and automatic repeal; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.
GA-2025-HB90.policyArea: CONSERVATION AND NATURAL RESOURCES, PROPERTY, REVENUE AND TAXATION
GA-2025-HB90.aiSummary: Georgia would raise the maximum acreage a property can have and still get a special tax break for bona fide conservation use land, which is land kept in conservation use. It affects property owners who want that lower tax treatment. The law was signed and takes effect on January 1, 2027.

GA-2025-HB1090.title: Echols County; Board of Commissioners; county commissioners shall be elected from the county at large; provide
GA-2025-HB1090.summary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend an Act revising, superseding, and consolidating the laws creating and governing the Board of Commissioners of Echols County, approved February 3, 1953 (Ga. L. 1953, Jan.-Feb. Sess., p. 2054), as amended, particularly by an Act approved April 11, 2022 (Ga. L. 2022, p.5446), so as to provide that all of the county commissioners shall be elected from the county at large; to repeal the commission district plan; to provide for continuation in office of current members; to provide for related matters; to provide an effective date; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.
committees: Senate State and Local Governmental Operations
GA-2025-HB1090.aiSummary: The law changes how Echols County commissioners are chosen. It moves all county commissioner races to countywide elections, instead of using commission districts, and lets current members stay in office until their terms end. It takes effect on January 1, 2027.

GA-2025-SR624.aiSummary: The resolution honors Officer Drew Haynes Brown and dedicates an intersection in Cobb County in his memory. It is a formal statement by lawmakers, not a law that sets new rules. It became Act 500 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB587.title: Offenses Against Public Health and Morals; the establishment of an animal cruelty database; provide
GA-2025-SB587.summary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend Article 1 of Chapter 12 of Title 16 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to general provisions regarding offenses against public health and morals, so as to provide for the establishment of an animal cruelty database; to provide for purpose and funding; to require the Prosecuting Attorneys' Council of the State of Georgia to create, administer, and maintain such database; to provide for minimum requirements; to provide for reporting and forms; to provide for related matters; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.

GA-2025-SB587.aiSummary: Georgia law creates an animal cruelty database. The Prosecuting Attorneys' Council of Georgia would create, run, and keep it, with rules for what it must include and how reports and forms are handled. It became law as Act 498 and takes effect July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB447.summary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend Chapter 7 of Title 12 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to control of soil erosion and sedimentation, so as to revise provisions regarding denial or nonacceptance of permits; to amend Chapter 60 of Title 36 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to provisions applicable to counties and municipal corporations, so as to provide general provisions for counties and municipalities regarding the acceptance, denial, or nonacceptance of certain permits; to require local issuing authorities to provide rejected permit applicants with a written list of reasons for denial within specified time frames; to provide definitions; to provide for related matters; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.

GA-2025-SB447.aiSummary: The law changes how local officials handle some permits tied to soil erosion and sediment control. GA-2025-SB293.summary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend Code Section 40-2-85.1 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to license plates for certain veterans, so as to increase the number of free license plates issued to certain veterans; to provide for related matters; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.

GA-2025-SB216.title: Georgia Judicial Retirement System; membership in the system for individuals employed as the director of the Prosecuting Attorneys Qualifications Commission; provide
GA-2025-SB216.summary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend Chapter 23 of Title 47 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to the Georgia Judicial Retirement System, so as to provide for membership in the system for individuals employed as the director of the Prosecuting Attorneys Qualifications Commission; to provide for an election for such current employees; to provide for transfer of funds; to provide for payment of actuarial costs; to provide for transfer of membership service; to provide for earnable monthly compensation for purposes of contributions and benefit amounts; to provide for applicability; to provide for related matters; to provide conditions for an effective date and automatic repeal; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.
GA-2025-SB216.aiSummary: The law lets people hired as the director of the Prosecuting Attorneys Qualifications Commission join the Georgia Judicial Retirement System. It also covers an option for current workers, moving funds, paying the system’s cost, and counting some past service and pay for retirement benefits. The law took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB146.summary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend Titles 31, 36, and 44 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to health, local government, and property, respectively, so as to provide regulations and protections of cemeteries and burial grounds; to revise procedures concerning the issuance of permits for the disinterment and reinterment of human remains; to provide definitions; to provide statutory construction; to conform cross-references; to provide for related matters; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.

GA-2025-SB146.aiSummary: The law updates state rules for cemeteries and burial grounds. It also changes how permits are handled for moving human remains from one burial place to another and adds definitions for some terms. It became Act 486 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HB1097.summary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend Title 37 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to mental health, so as to provide for criminal background, license status, and registry checks for owners, applicants, and employees of certain mental health facilities; to provide for the Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Disabilities to submit fingerprints to the Federal Bureau of Investigation and Georgia Crime Information Center for the purpose of background checks to find disqualifying records; to provide for maintenance of personnel files; to provide for procedures relating to applicants or employees with ineligible determinations; to provide for definitions; to provide for related matters; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.

GA-2025-HB1097.aiSummary: Georgia now requires certain mental health facilities to check the criminal record, license status, and registry status of owners, applicants, and employees. GA-2026SS-SR13.summary: A RESOLUTION recognizing and commending Tayvian D. Allen; and for other purposes.
GA-2026SS-SR13.aiSummary: The Georgia Senate adopted a resolution to recognize and commend Tayvian D. Allen. It is a formal statement of recognition for him.

GA-2026SS-SB6.title: Stephens County; ad valorem taxes; homestead property determined annually for the special district based upon the proceeds of a new Local Homestead Option Sales Tax (LHOST); provide homestead exemption
GA-2026SS-SB6.summary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to provide a homestead exemption from Stephens County ad valorem taxes in the amount of the assessed value of the homestead property determined annually for the special district based upon the proceeds of a new Local Homestead Option Sales Tax (LHOST) to be imposed within the special district conterminous with Stephens County; to provide for definitions; to specify the terms and conditions of the exemption and the procedures relating thereto; to provide for applicability; to provide for compliance with constitutional requirements and the provisions of Article 2C of Chapter 8 of Title 48 of the O.C.G.A.; to provide for a referendum, effective dates, automatic repeal, mandatory execution of election, and judicial remedies regarding failure to comply; to provide for related matters; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.
committees: Senate State and Local Governmental Operations

votes.motion: MOTION TO RECONSIDER LOCAL CONSENT CALENDAR

GA-2026SS-SB6.aiSummary: The bill would create a homestead tax break for homes in Stephens County. The break would match the assessed value of the home, based on money from a new local sales tax in a special district that covers the county. It would also set rules for how the exemption works and when it applies.

GA-2026SS-SB10.title: Sales and Use Taxes; any existing special district option sales and use tax (FLOST) cease to be imposed and levied immediately prior to the imposition of any local homestead option sales tax (LHOST); require
GA-2026SS-SB10.summary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend Chapter 8 of Title 48 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to sales and use taxes, so as to require that any existing special district option sales and use tax (FLOST) cease to be imposed and levied immediately prior to the imposition of any local homestead option sales tax (LHOST) within the special district conterminous with the same county; to revise the timing for the commencement of the LHOST; to provide for an effective date; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.
GA-2026SS-SB10.aiSummary: The bill would require any existing special district sales tax (FLOST) to stop right before a local homestead option sales tax (LHOST) starts in the same county district. It would also change when the LHOST begins. It includes an effective date and would repeal conflicting laws.
